ian (People Ops): Hey team — Lina asked whether taking a 401(k) loan will affect eligibility for our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) or other benefits enrollment windows. tagging @marta and @diego to confirm :wave:
marta (Benefits): Short answer: generally no, a 401(k) loan itself doesn't disqualify you from ESPP or benefits enrollment. but two things to watch: (1) cashflow — loan repayments reduce net pay so you might hit contribution limits for ESPP / FSA decisions, and (2) termination rules — outstanding loans treated as distribution at termination could affect taxable income the year you leave.
diego (Payroll): Ops notes: loan repayments are a separate payroll deduction code (`RD401K_LOAN`) and don't touch ESPP payroll elections. But if someone reduces their elective deferral to cover a loan repayment, that will change pre-tax contribution amounts. For FP: if loan causes low net pay and triggers minimum wage/benefit eligibility thresholds, payroll should be notified.
lina: what about open enrollment timing? if i start a loan now, can i still make changes during next OE?
marta (Benefits): Yes — open enrollment changes are independent of having a loan. You can enroll, change elections, or waive benefits at OE regardless of a loan. Just remember loan repayment continues until it's paid or vendor/agreement changes.
ian (People Ops): Any vendor paperwork implications we should tell folks?
diego (Payroll): Vendor (AtlasRetire) will send a loan approval with repayment schedule and a transaction ID. employee should forward that email to payroll@redwood.example before payroll cutoff. payroll uses the transaction ID to map the `RD401K_LOAN` deduction. If they miss the cutoff, first deduction is delayed one pay period.
marta (Benefits): Additional items employees often miss:
• Loans outstanding at termination: Atlas may treat unpaid balance as distribution. Get a written note from vendor if you plan a leave/exit.
• ESPP contribution impacts: If you enroll in ESPP, ESPP contributions are separate post-tax payroll deductions; verify combined deductions don't cause cashflow issues.
• FSA impacts: If you rely on FSA reimbursements, remember those are run-rate benefits and won't offset immediate loan repayments.
